brief: Goldman's Brian Garrett (Weekend Prep, Nov 20) quantifies the Q4 2018 comparison clients keep raising, measuring every major market's move since the S&P's Oct 6 peak against the 2018 drawdown. Equities, especially tech, have moved roughly in step with 2018 (Nasdaq 100 69% of its 2018 drawdown, S&P 42%, Russell 2000 24%), so extrapolating that path implies another 12% S&P downside to about 6,294, with the low due around early January on the same trading-day clock. Credit and the Fed have not followed: CDX IG and HY spreads have widened only 15% and 28% as much as in 2018, the front end of rates is not pricing a policy pivot, and the Fed is still hiking into hot CPI (Goldman expects a third hike in March) with no backstop signaled. Havens inverted too, with gold and the yen falling instead of hedging as in 2018. Separately, Goldman's Vol Views note reads dealer positioning as stressed (Panic Index near 9) but sees clients starting to sell skew rather than buy calls, and recommends QQQ call spreads, a staples hedge and cheap AI-bounce calls. A separate chart set shows 2026's biggest first-half winners becoming the worst second-half laggards.
